title: High Throughput SARS-COV-2, PMMOV, and BCoV Quantification Using Digital RT-PCR
author: Aaron Topol (Verily Life Sciences)
materials: Retrieve all kit components from the One-Step RT-ddPCR advanced kit for probes from the -20 °C freezer and thaw the components On ice . One-Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #186-4021

Briefly vortex One-Step RT supermix for Probes (Yellow Tube), Reverse Transcriptase (Orange Tube), and DTT (Grey Tube) to mix contents then briefly spin with the benchtop centrifuge. One-Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #186-4021

For each assay, remove a white cold block from the freezer and place a new Bio-Rad ddPCR 96-well Plate in it. Note that these steps may be completed with a liquid handling robot. We use the BRAVO system.

Bring the BioRad ddPCR plate with Master Mix and samples to the Bio-Rad PX1 PCR Plate Sealer and place it in the metal carrier inside the plate sealer. Do not store the metal carrier inside the plate sealer, as it will become warm and warm the samples during sealing.
For the Droplet Plate: label a new Bio-Rad ddPCR™ 96-Well Plate and place it in the black cooling block.

steps.title: Retrieve positive control aliquots
steps.instruction: Retrieve ddPCR positive‑control aliquots (50 copies µL⁻¹ gRNA and 100 copies µL⁻¹ BCoV and PMMoV gene‑block) from the –80 °C freezer and thaw on ice.

steps.title: Thaw frozen RNA plates (if needed)
steps.instruction: For re‑running frozen plates only, thaw the RNA storage plate on ice, ensure the plate is sealed, briefly vortex, and centrifuge to mix the samples.

steps.title: Keep RNA on ice & prevent contamination
steps.instruction: Keep all extracted RNA samples on ice or on a cold block at all times. Use freshly prepared nuclease‑free water, change gloves frequently, and wipe down the work surface and pipettes with clean water because the PMMoV assay is highly sensitive to contamination.

steps.title: Prepare fresh nuclease‑free water stock
steps.instruction: Pour nuclease‑free water from a 50 mL Ambion bottle into a 5 mL Eppendorf tube to create a fresh working stock.

steps.title: Prepare SARS‑CoV‑2 master mix
steps.instruction: Store all master‑mix components on ice. In a 2 mL Eppendorf tube, assemble the SARS‑CoV‑2 triplex master mix (targets N, S, ORF1a) according to the provided table, using the 20× SARS‑CoV‑2 Primer/Probe Mix (primers and probes at the concentrations listed in the protocol). Store the prepared master mix on ice. Do not multiplex with a high‑copy target such as PMMoV.

steps.title: Prepare BCoV/PMMoV master mix
steps.instruction: Store all components on ice. Briefly vortex the One‑Step RT Supermix for Probes (yellow tube) and Reverse Transcriptase (orange tube), spin briefly, and thaw the DTT (grey tube). In a separate 2 mL Eppendorf tube, assemble the BCoV/PMMoV master mix according to the provided table, using the 20× BCoV/PMMoV Primer/Probe Mix (primers and probes at the concentrations listed). Store the prepared master mix on ice.

steps.title: Dilute RNA 1:100 for BCoV/PMMoV
steps.instruction: Dilute each RNA sample 1:100 for the BCoV/PMMoV RT‑ddPCR assay because of the expected high target concentration. Dilution can be performed manually or with a liquid‑handling robot (e.g., Agilent Bravo).

steps.title: Prepare diluted RNA plate
steps.instruction: Using a new reagent reservoir, pipette 198 µL nuclease‑free water into every well of an Eppendorf twin.tec PCR plate labeled “100× RNA Dilution”. Then add 2 µL of each stock RNA sample to the corresponding well. Seal the plate, vortex briefly on a bench‑top plate vortexer, spin down in an Axygen plate centrifuge, and store on ice until use.

steps.title: Add master mix to ddPCR plate
steps.instruction: Using a fresh reagent reservoir, pipette 16.5 µL of the appropriate master mix (SARS‑CoV‑2 or BCoV/PMMoV) into each well of each ddPCR plate.

steps.title: Transfer samples and controls to ddPCR plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 5.5 µL of diluted RNA from columns 1‑10 of the RNA plate into the same columns of the ddPCR plate. Transfer 5.5 µL of extraction‑control RNA from column 12 of the RNA plate into column 11 of the ddPCR plate. Add 5.5 µL of no‑template control (water) to wells A‑G of column 12. Add 5.5 µL of ddPCR positive control to well H12 (add manually even if using a robot). For the SARS‑CoV‑2 assay add SARS‑CoV‑2 genomic RNA; for the PMMoV/BCoV assay add the corresponding gene‑block positive control. Note that column 11 of the ddPCR plate receives column 12 of the extraction plate.

steps.title: Seal and vortex/ddPCR plate
steps.instruction: Align a PCR‑Plate Heat‑Seal foil on the ddPCR plate with the red line facing up, press the green “seal” button, vortex briefly on a bench‑top plate vortexer, then spin down in the Axygen plate centrifuge.

steps.title: Store ddPCR plate before droplet generation
steps.instruction: Place the sealed ddPCR plate on a white cold block or keep it on ice until droplet generation.

steps.title: Set up AutoDG droplet generator
steps.instruction: On the AutoDG, select “configure plate” and highlight all columns. Load three DG32 cartridge plates and two tip boxes (lids removed) onto the deck; icons turn red then green when correctly placed. Place the sealed, vortexed, centrifuged ddPCR plate in the Sample Plate position. Remove the AutoDG cooling block from the freezer and insert it into the Droplet Plate slot.

steps.title: Generate droplets and prepare second plate
steps.instruction: Click “Generate Droplets” and allow ~00:45:00 for droplet generation. While the SARS‑CoV‑2 plate is generating droplets, set up the PMMoV/BCoV plate in the same manner.

steps.title: Seal droplet plate and run PCR
steps.instruction: When droplet generation finishes, open the lid, remove the droplet plate from the black cold block, and place it in the metal carrier inside the plate sealer. Align a PCR‑Plate Heat‑Seal foil (red line up) and press the green “seal” button (do NOT vortex now). Place the sealed plate in the thermocycler, select the appropriate program (SARS‑CoV‑2 or BCoV/PMMoV) from the protocol table, run the cycling conditions, then store the plate at 4 °C (in the thermocycler, on ice, or in a refrigerator) until droplet reading.

steps.title: Prepare droplet reader and load template
steps.instruction: Open the left drawer of the QX200 droplet reader; verify sufficient droplet‑reader oil and that the waste bottle is not overfull. Load the template from the previous plate of the same assay, confirm dye/absorbance settings, assign sample names to wells, and save with a descriptive new plate name.

steps.title: Run droplet reading in Quantasoft
steps.instruction: Secure the plate in the droplet reader (stage, metal brace, press black plastic tabs), click “Run” in Quantasoft, confirm the dialog, and keep the settings at “Columns” and “FAM/HEX”.

steps.title: Analyze SARS‑CoV‑2 data
steps.instruction: Open the .qlp file. In the Plate Editor tab, select all wells, choose Assay Information → “Probe Mix Triplex”, apply the settings. If sample names are missing, add them now. If any wells must be excluded, select them and click “Clear Selected Well”. On the 2D Amplitude tab, with all wells highlighted, select the Threshold Cluster Mode Graph Tool and draw 2D thresholds around each cluster. Verify that each well contains >10 000 droplets; clear any well that does not. Select “Merged Wells” on the left, then click the Table Menu button on the right of the Well Data table and choose “Export to CSV”.

steps.title: Analyze BCoV/PMMoV data
steps.instruction: Open the .qlp file (if a new file). In the Plate Editor tab, select all wells, choose Assay Information → “Simplex/Duplex”, apply. On the 1D Amplitude tab, with all wells highlighted, click the Threshold Multiple Wells button to set automatic thresholds: BCoV = 5000, PMMoV = 1700. Verify that thresholds correctly separate positive and negative droplets and that each well has >10 000 droplets; clear any problematic well. Select “Merged Wells” on the left, then click the Table Menu button and choose “Export to CSV”, saving the file.

steps.title: Calculate copies per gram dry weight
steps.instruction:
Use the concentration reported by QuantaSoft (gc µL⁻¹ reaction) from the CSV. Convert to copies per gram dry weight using the formula: 

gc µL⁻¹ × B ÷ A × C ÷ Z, where B = 20 µL total reaction volume, A = 5 µL template volume, C = 60 µL elution volume, Z = 0.0225 g wet weight solids per extraction well (derived from 300 µL of a suspension containing 75 mg mL⁻¹ wet solids). Adjust for the measured percent solids (typical 5‑30 %). Verify calculations against instrument‑specific reporting conventions.
